newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Simeon to bid for Austvin.
newsitem.headline: Simeon to bid for Austvin.

text.p: Simeon Wines Ltd said on Tuesday it intended to seek a merger with fellow winemaker Australian Vintage Ltd by means of a share and cash offer, valuing Austvin at about A$111 million.
Simeon said the offer would be four Simeon shares plus A$3.60 cash for every five Austvin shares.
Based on Simeon's closing share price on Tuesday of A$2.86, the offer equates to about A$3.01 per Austvin share, Simeon said.

Austvin shares last traded on Monday at a 12-month high of A$2.85, valuing the group at A$105.19 million, before being suspended at its own request on Tuesday because it had received an indication of the possibility of a bid.
Simeon said a succesful merger would create Australia's fourth largest winemaker by volume.
Simeon said it would fund the cash component of the offer partly from existing facilities and partly from new facilities offered by Simeon's bankers.
"We have always viewed a merger with Austvin as being a sensible combining of assets and resources," Simeon chairman John Branson said.
"It has long been forecast that Australian winery capacity is likely to be severely stretched in the next few years," he said in a statement.
"We believe that Simeon should focus on this sector of its business with some vigour.
"We have recently been unable to satisfy demand for bulk wine both domestically and internationally," Branson said.
"A merger of the two businesses will create the critical mass to enable us to fulfil customer demand requirements at an earlier stage than if we continued to operate independently," he said.
He said assets of a merged group would include:

- two large and efficient wine processing facilities with current capacity of 100,000 tonnes processing 12 percent of Australia's wine grape crop with access to fruit from Australian's largest grape growing regions.
- 3,000 acres of vineyards in the Padthaway, Cowra, Riverland and Sunraysia districts.
The offer carries a number of conditions including:
- Simeon becoming entitled to proceed with compulsory acquisition of any minority which does not accept the offer.
- The successful raising of A$9 million by June 30 from Austvin's recently announced vineyard investment scheme.
- The approval of Australia's Foreign Investment Review Board.
